description: Dark teal plates, always beaded with water. The thing that grew it has not surfaced yet.
lore: Grading is comparison. You hold the stone against the creature — that is the entire method, and it works, because one kind of creature leaves one kind of stone and the trade has spent a long time pairing them off. There is nothing to hold this one against. So the graders read it backwards instead, out of what it does, and every one of them arrives at the same sentence and none of them enjoy saying it aloud: whatever reached the bottom of this had no particular reason to come up.

It is heavy for its size and plated like something's back, overlapping dark teal with a bright seam at every edge, warm as any stone in the trade and beaded all over with water it has no business having. Worn, you swim like a thing that lives down there. And you breathe. Not hold your breath longer — breathe, for as long as you care to, which is the part sellers say twice.

[[characters/a6d7323d|Gunnar]] uses one for work. A Turn put four miles of the low road under water eleven years ago and he has walked the whole of it since, along the bottom, correcting a map he has not been asked for. He has said one thing about the stone, to one person, and it had nothing to do with the map: down there he does not think about breathing at all, and twice he has come up only because the light went, and he could not afterwards say how long he had been under. He does not speculate about what grew it. He has noticed what it does to a man only borrowing the habit, and he has gone back down anyway.
gm_notes: Unbound stone, handled as a grading problem rather than a provenance hunt — the opal, the moss plate, the frost rune and the woodgrain have between them used the price floor, the cheap oddity, the unmarkable mark and the empty category, so this one turns on method: with no creature to compare against, the only reading available is the power, and the power reads as a life spent not surfacing. Nothing is asserted to exist. Gunnar is at work here, not investigating; the cold end is what the stone does to the borrower, and it is left unresolved on purpose.
